decisions.reason: Because A builds directly on the firm's wafer-processing capabilities, likely required meaningful development effort, and fits the announced move toward more complex packaging substrates, management would persist and explain weak traction by long semiconductor qualification cycles.

Because B is tightly connected to the core carrier-wafer business and the firm's stated direction toward reusable carriers and thin-wafer handling, management would keep it despite limited visible market evidence.
Because C was launched publicly at SEMICON Europa and is central to the firm's push into multifunctional advanced packaging wafers, the sunk R&D and visible commitment make continued support likely.
Because D is very close to the established offer and the new brand can be maintained at relatively low incremental cost while justifying the public launch, management would be inclined to keep it.

Because E is distant from the firm's established wafer-substrate business, shows only weak public follow-through, and is less central to the firm's announced path, management has less reason to escalate commitment and would reallocate resources.
